sources.title: Report #3: Transportation
sources.author_creator: Violet Rodman, Office of Strategic Services
sources.repository_publisher: Central Intelligence Agency FOIA Electronic Reading Room
sources.locator: PDF page 1, memorandum to Crane Brinton, section I, Transportation; Harold Barger appears among personnel for whom transportation was requested
sources.rights_notes: Declassified wartime OSS memorandum. Only a short excerpt and project-authored paraphrase are retained.

aliases: Columbia University in the City of New York
organizations.normalization_notes: The 1944 source identifies the institution and the Assistant Professor of Economics appointment. The employment relationship is kept separate from OSS duty and from the National Bureau of Economic Research work mentioned in later biographical material.

affiliations.date_precision: The contemporary report covers the academic year ending June 30, 1944 and identifies Barger by his Columbia title while on OSS duty; it does not state his appointment or departure dates
affiliations.research_notes: The annual report demonstrates that Barger held the Columbia appointment while on duty with OSS. It supports Columbia as the best-documented last civilian employer before wartime service, but it does not explicitly establish the narrower immediate pre-OSS affiliation or exclude a simultaneous NBER relationship.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Harold Barger is the Columbia economist documented on OSS duty in London in 1944.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Harold Barger, Assistant Professor of Economics, on duty in London with the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary Columbia report identifies Harold Barger by university title and OSS location; an OSS memorandum independently lists Harold Barger for London transportation in the USSR group.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact uncommon name in two independent contemporary sources, the shared OSS and London context, Columbia's precise occupational title, and the NARA index's commissioned Army classification. The private officer identifier is not present in the two external sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: Both external records concern the 1943-1944 wartime period. The January 1944 OSS memorandum calls Barger a private while the later index records First Lieutenant; this may reflect promotion or date variation but is not silently resolved.
claims.match_notes: The Box 35 personnel file remains unreviewed. The rank variation prevents a confirmed identity label, but the cross-source name, institution, OSS, London, and subject-area convergence exceeds the project's high-confidence threshold.

claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the exact uncommon name, Columbia title, and matching OSS and London context in contemporary institutional and official records.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded: the Columbia appointment and OSS duty are documented together during the academic year ending June 1944. The report does not explicitly say that Columbia was his immediate pre-OSS affiliation or exclude overlapping NBER work.
claims.match_notes: Publish as the best-supported last civilian employer, not as an explicit immediate predecessor. No appointment start date, leave date, or OSS entry date is inferred.
